![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217747/assets/98bc6f2ea4d71368226f0f784d629e98949e07005bc08158206de35a87bea520.png)

Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r=3-3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $\frac{3\pi }{2}\le \theta \le 2\pi ,$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=3-3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{3\pi }{2}$ and ${\theta }_{2}=2\pi $, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }(3-3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }(9-18\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +9{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{9}{2}{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{9}{2}(\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }+\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}(\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }+\frac{1}{2}(\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}{2}\,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi })) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}(\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }+\frac{1}{2}\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}{4}\,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }) \\  & =\frac{27}{4}\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }-9\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }+\frac{9\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )}{8}\,{|}_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{27}{4}(2\pi -\frac{3\pi }{2})-9(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))+\frac{9}{8}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )) \\  & =\frac{27\pi }{8}-9+\frac{9}{8}(0) \\  & =\frac{27\pi -72}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
